question.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the distance between $f(t)=7t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-2$ with respect to the inner product.

current_example.problem:
Let $V = \Bbb R_1[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $1$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
\langle p(t), q(t) \rangle = p(0)q(0) + p(1)q(1),
$$

find the distance between $p(t) = 4t + 2$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t) = t$ with respect to the inner product.
current_example.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{ q(t) \}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)}{q(0)^{2}+q(1)^{2}}\cdot q(t) \\  & =\frac{(2)(0)+(6)(1)}{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\cdot t \\  & =6t.\end{aligned}
$$

The distance between $p(t) = 4t + 2$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t) = t$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖p(t)-{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)‖ \\  & =‖(4t+2)-6t‖ \\  & =‖-2t+2‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨-2t+2,\text{ }-2t+2⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨-2t+2,\text{ }-2t+2⟩ & =(-2t+2){|}_{0}\cdot (-2t+2){|}_{0}+(-2t+2){|}_{1}\cdot (-2t+2){|}_{1} \\  & =(-2(0)+2)^{2}+(-2(1)+2)^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+{0}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d = \sqrt{4} = 2.$
